claim: Live multi-turn model sessions re-bill the whole conversation on every turn. Per-answer estimates that ignore it run several times low; once the estimate must state its basis (turns x re-billed context), it holds within a few percent. Splitting into one-answer sessions saves less than expected when each session has a fixed set-up of several turns.

metric.what: Estimated against actual cost per answer of one live model test run, as reported by the master (not measured by the analyst).

recordKinds: a report from the master, not a record
countedFrom.machine: one Windows 11 machine; one master, 8 orchestrators, about 50 short-lived workers, one person
versions: agent harness as installed in the period (exact version not recorded)

proposedChange: AI tests that do not need long context run as one-question sessions in parallel; estimates are computed from measured cost per turn including re-billed context, checked against the first session before the rest run; alarm when cost per answer exceeds 2x estimate or a session exceeds 5 turns without a stated reason. Count the per-session set-up turns as the floor: short sessions mainly buy predictability and no runaway growth, and save money only above that floor.
whyItGeneralises: Re-billing of the whole conversation per turn is how multi-turn model sessions are priced generally; an estimate that ignores it is low on any fleet.
limits: Two runs on one stack: the 4x overrun (master's figures) and a 4-case validation whose manifest the monitor read (estimate 0.055, measured 0.053 USD per answer).
